column4: Tariffs on pharmaceuticals, more information on deal with UK: The White House issues a proclamation and fact sheet imposing Section 232 tariffs on patented pharmaceuticals and their ingredients, including a 100 percent tariff, with implementation in 120 days for large companies and 180 days for smaller companies. column4: US-Taiwan trade deal: The Commerce Department issues a fact sheet announcing details of a US trade agreement with Taiwan. column4: Tariffs and exemptions for semiconductors as well as tax on AI chip exports to China: The White House issues a proclamation and fact sheet invoking Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 to impose import tariffs on semiconductors. The announcement exempts semiconductor tariffs for particular end uses in the US, such as data centers. Simultaneously, the Commerce Department publishes a revision to its license review policy for exports of certain artificial intelligence (AI) chips from Nvidia and AMD destined for China. The new policy requires chip testing at a lab in the US; the requirement to import in order to re-export to China allows the US to apply a 25 percent import tariff on those specific chips. (The legal argument is that this is being applied as an import tariff and not a US export tax, the latter of which is inconsistent with Article I, Section 9 of the US Constitution.)
